ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

2. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

3. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

5. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

6. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. went

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

10. When practising Speaking Fluency: pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

11. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. blue

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension.

2. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions.

5. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Class: Collective Nouns/ Reflexive Pronouns.

6. D — went

7. C — Where is the library?

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 3.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional Writing: Filling Forms.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency: pronunciation.

11. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

12. C — run

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 4.3.1 Word Class: Possessive Pronouns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 4.4.1 Functional Writing: Friendly Letter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
